Manuel's answers to the first grilling round on this ticket, 2026-09-30, word for word, so they don't have to be remembered or rediscovered. The round was asked after the research in [Research how wording and missing context shape a reader's response](https://github.com/Zenoctra/factory918/issues/154) landed. Claude's questions, in short:

- **Q1**: what makes a rule binding (one the reader may not overrule by itself): (a) what it is about, (b) who owns it, (c) both, (d) case by case.
- **Q2**: how the writer passes on what it knows about the route: (a) leave it out, (b) as a resource with its reason, (c) as a default the reader may override.
- **Q3**: rules that bound how a task is finished (reporting bars, caps, citation gates): (a) the reader reports everything with its own confidence and severity, a later step applies any bar, and every brief leaves room to report what was noticed outside the task; (b) keep bars, reworded as ranking; (c) case by case.
- **Q4**: one mechanism for departing from a rule, in place of the five the factory has now.
- **Q5**: whether cost or time may justify limiting the route.

EOF

cat <<'EOF'
